Update rehire rule for Medical
-	if rehired within 13 weeks, the date of rehire eligibility applies; after 13 weeks, it is FOMF 60 days.
For K2, the rehires are treated as follows

•	If rehired within 30 days (4 weeks), the employee should be reinstated to prior coverage
•	If rehired between 4 weeks and 13 weeks,

o	offer benefits on the rehire date if the break in employment is less than the prior employment duration
o	offer benefits with a new hire waiting period, if the break in employment is longer than the prior employment duration
•	If rehired after 13 weeks, offer benefits with the new hire waiting period.

In our system, for both the API and file feeds, rehires are always handled manually, one by one. Someone must go into the employee record and click the rehire button. For K2, every time we have a rehire, the team should review these rules and apply them accordingly.

These are the steps to handle Rehires for K2


•	If rehired within 30 days (4 weeks),

o	Rehire the employee in BenJ and enroll him in the same benefits he had before. He doesn’t need to re-enroll. In the system, the rehire rule is set up as: if rehired within 13 weeks, coverage starts on the rehire date. So, when you rehire, it automatically uses the rehire date as the effective date, and we should just enroll him in the same benefits he had before as of the rehire date. Also assign it to the product to expire the to-do list. Because the K2 doc says they should not be allowed to make changes without a life event.
•	If rehired between 4 and 13 weeks

o	If the break in employment is less than the prior employment,

?	Then you just rehire the employee, and the within-13-weeks rule will be applied by the system, and coverage starts on the rehire date. The employee will receive the email and log in to complete the enrollment.
o	If the break in employment is longer than the prior employment,

?	Do not rehire the employee; assign that to the product. We will need to apply the new-hire waiting period to ensure the effective date is shown correctly

When processing a rehire, the system automatically uses the rehire date as the effective date. The employee should be manually enrolled in the same benefits they had prior to termination, effective as of the rehire date.
Also, assign this record to the Product team so they can expire/end the to-do list. According to the K2 documentation, employees should not be allowed to make benefit changes unless they have a qualifying life event.
Issue: In these scenarios, the rehire activation email is triggered automatically. The current workaround is to temporarily disable the email notification before processing the rehire and then use this approach only for these specific cases.

2.	Rehires Between 4 and 13 Weeks
•	If the break in employment is shorter than the employee's prior period of employment:
o	Rehire the employee as usual.
o	The system will automatically apply the within-13-weeks rule, and coverage will become effective on the rehire date.
o	The employee will receive the rehire activation email and can log in to complete their enrollment.
•	If the break in employment is longer than the employee's prior period of employment:
o	Do not rehire the employee.
o	Assign the case to the Product team.
o	A new-hire waiting period must be applied to ensure the correct benefit effective date is calculated and displayed.

Two configuration changes are needed for ATK Energy Group based on a discrepancy identified between the BenJ system setup and the carrier (Principal) configuration, confirmed by the client contact Jennifer Carroll (TrueNorth Companies) on July 24, 2026.

1. Overage Dependent Rule — Update for All Plans (Principal and Medical/BCBS of OK)

The overage dependent rule in BenJ is currently configured as "When Dependent Turns 26," but Principal is applying "End of Month After 26th Birthday." This discrepancy was identified when Jennifer Grahn's dependent, Gillian Grahn (DOB 03/30/2000), was removed from plans effective 03/30/2026 in BenJ, while Principal's effective removal date was 04/01/2026. Jennifer Carroll confirmed the correct rule is end-of-month after the dependent turns 26. This same correction should also be applied to the Medical (BCBS of OK) plan, which is currently configured with the same "When Dependent Turns 26" rule.

Action: Change overage dependent rule from "When Dependent Turns 26" to "End of Month After 26th Birthday" for all applicable plans including Principal and Medical (BCBS of OK).

2. Voluntary Life Spouse Age Reduction Rule — Update from Plan Anniversary to Birthday

The age reduction rule for Voluntary Life Spouse (and Employee) coverage in BenJ is currently set to apply on the Plan Anniversary. However, Principal applies the age reduction on the dependent's birthday. This was identified for employee Joe Hulett (EE #2886), whose spouse's date of birth is 01/16/1961 and turned 65 on 01/16/2026. Principal already reduced her coverage on the birthday, but BenJ's current setup would not apply the reduction until the next plan anniversary, 01/01/2027. 

Jennifer Carroll confirmed the age reduction should occur on the Birthday to match Principal.

Action: Change Voluntary Life Spouse (and Employee) age reduction rule trigger from Plan Anniversary to Birthday.
